invariant_repaired.description: fabric.interface.authority_permits() previously ignored AuthorityContext.expires_at entirely; an expired grant still satisfied the check. Fixed: authority_permits() now parses expires_at (when set) and denies whenever evaluation_time >= expires_at.

expiry_semantics_selected.expires_at_greater_than_evaluation_time: ELIGIBLE, subject to all existing authority checks (capability_id must still be in granted_capability_ids)
expiry_semantics_selected.expires_at_equal_to_evaluation_time: REJECTED (fail-closed boundary: evaluation_time >= expires_at is expired), per operator's explicitly preferred semantic
expiry_semantics_selected.timestamp_representation: No new representation invented. expires_at continues to be an Optional[str] in the pre-existing _now() format ('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', UTC/Zulu). It is parsed via datetime.strptime() using that exact format and made explicitly UTC-aware via .replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc), since the trailing 'Z' in every value this module has ever written denotes UTC. No naive/aware ambiguity exists in stored data because the module has only ever produced one string shape via _now(); the ambiguity risk that does exist is at the evaluation_time call boundary (see below).
expiry_semantics_selected.naive_vs_aware_handling: authority_permits() gained an optional evaluation_time: Optional[datetime] parameter (defaults to datetime.now(timezone.utc) when omitted, preserving real-wall-clock behavior for the one production call site). If a caller supplies a naive (tzinfo=None) evaluation_time, the function raises FabricError explicitly rather than attempting a comparison whose outcome would depend on an unstated timezone assumption -- this is the naive/aware ambiguity surfaced explicitly, as required, rather than silently resolved.
expiry_semantics_selected.malformed_expiry_handling: If expires_at is set but does not parse against the exact _now() format (datetime.strptime raises ValueError), authority_permits() returns False (denies) rather than falling back to string comparison or treating it as non-expiring. This is the fail-closed handling of 'uncertainty could accidentally grant authority.'

unresolved_risks: evaluation_time defaults to datetime.now(timezone.utc) when omitted by a caller; the one production call site (fabric/interface.py process_remote_capability_request(), line ~578) calls authority_permits() with two positional arguments and therefore uses real wall-clock time -- this was not changed, and no test exercises that exact call site's expiry behavior end-to-end (only authority_permits() itself is tested directly with an injected evaluation_time). A future microphase could add an end-to-end test through process_remote_capability_request() with a real expired context.

expires_at remains an unvalidated free-text Optional[str] at construction time (AuthorityContext has no __post_init__ check on this field, matching architecture/authority-map.md's prior observation about granted_by being free-text too) -- malformed values are only caught when authority_permits() is actually called, not at grant-construction time. This mission did not add construction-time validation because doing so was outside the bounded surface (authority_permits() itself) and risked expanding scope into AuthorityContext's constructor semantics.
no timezone other than UTC is or was ever supported; this is consistent with the pre-existing _now() convention, not a new limitation introduced by this mission.
